run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T05:03:07Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by gateway-timeout errors on the proxy's inbound requests. In the 73-minute window from 04:03:07 to 05:16:08, the ingress spans of frontend-proxy accumulated 236.4 error-status spans while 23,687 were status-unset, and the sampled error spans carry http.status_code 504 with durations of ~15.0s. That 15s cutoff is the proxy giving up on its upstream: in the sampled traces the frontend's POST /api/checkout span, checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span and checkout's Kafka producer span 'orders publish' all take ~15.2-15.4s, while every other downstream span in the same traces (currency, payment, cart, email) completes in milliseconds. The slow producer step is the deepest bottleneck. Its onset is abrupt and coincides with the kafka Deployment being replaced: a new ReplicaSet with pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T05:00:36Z was created, the old broker pod was deleted at 05:00:38, checkout logged 'connect: connection refused' to kafka:9092 and 'circuit breaker is open' from 05:00:42 until it reconnected at 05:02:21, and the new broker performed its KRaft leader election at 05:02:02-05:02:05. Slow 'orders publish' spans (zero per minute up to 05:02:07) appear in the minute ending 05:03:07 and dominate thereafter, which is the same minute the alert fired. The kafka pod is not resource-starved (memory ~592-622MiB against a 900Mi limit, ~0.045 CPU cores after startup, 1.5% CPU throttling, no node pressure), so the restart of the broker and its fresh state is the supported trigger, while the exact broker-internal reason produce stays slow after reconnect remains unverified.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error signal is on its ingress spans: over 04:03:07-05:16:08, increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress"}) is 236.43 for status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR versus 23,687.29 for STATUS_CODE_UNSET, while its 'router frontend egress' spans show 0.0 error-status spans and 23,924.74 unset.

Across all services over the same window, the only large error-span count is frontend-proxy/ingress at 236.43; checkout 'orders publish' shows 14.70 error spans and everything else is 0 (for example frontend's GET, POST, POST /api/checkout, executing api route and grpc client spans all return 0 error spans).

The proxy's error volume rises over 5-minute buckets: 2.22 (04:43), 3.33 (04:48), 6.67 (04:53), 3.33 (04:58), 26.67 (05:03), 62.86 (05:08), 108.89 (05:13) error spans, against 3,247-3,815 unset ingress spans per bucket; the instant rate of ingress error spans over 5 minutes at 05:16:08 is 0.211/s, the same order as the alert's reported 0.4.

The sampled frontend-proxy ingress error spans are HTTP 504 with durations of 15,001,094us, 15,000,795us and 15,000,736us, and their 'router frontend egress' child spans last the same ~15.0s with http.status_code "0"; in the same trace the frontend POST /api/checkout span lasts 15.44s with http.status_code 200, checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder lasts 15.44s with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, and checkout's 'orders publish' span lasts 15.24s while currency/email/cart children take 17-100ms.

Long latency is confined to the checkout path: spans between 10s and 15s in 05:10-05:15 are frontend-proxy/ingress 67.5, frontend-proxy/'router frontend egress' 80.5, frontend POST 76.6, frontend POST /api/checkout 49.4, frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 49.4, checkout 'orders publish' 53.3 and checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 50.7, with cart, payment and recommendation at 0. Spans over 5s in 05:10-05:15 are frontend 496.9, checkout 256.6, frontend-proxy 246.6, accounting 6.2 and 0 for every other service.

checkout's 'orders publish' slowness starts abruptly at the kafka restart: the per-minute count of its spans longer than 10s is 0 for every minute returned up to and including 05:02:07, then 42 (05:03:07), 66, 56, 52, 66, 48, 78, 56, 70. The 5-minute fraction of 'orders publish' spans over 10s is 0 for 04:38-04:58 buckets, 0.157 for the bucket ending 05:03, 0.926 for 05:08 and 0.982 for 05:13; frontend POST /api/checkout tracks it (0.197, 0.946, 0.982).

The kafka Deployment was rolled at 05:00:36: a new ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 (revision 2) was created and scaled up, pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 was scheduled/created/started at 05:00:36-05:00:37, and the previous pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 was killed and deleted at 05:00:38 with kafka-ff7884766 scaled down 1->0.

The trigger for that rollout was a pod-template restart annotation, not a container-spec change: the new ReplicaSet's pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T05:00:36Z while the old ReplicaSet has none, and both ReplicaSets carry the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka, identical command/args/ports, identical KAFKA_* env and identical resources (limits cpu 400m / memory 900Mi).

checkout's Kafka producer failed against the restarted broker: log lines from the checkout pod show 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused', 'client/metadata no available broker to send metadata request to' and 'Failed to write message: kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open' between 05:00:42 and 05:02:15, then 'Connected to broker at kafka:9092' and 'producer/broker/1 state change to [open] on orders/0' at 05:02:21.

The new kafka broker spent its startup as a fresh single-node KRaft broker: its logs show Raft transitions to Unattached, CandidateState and Leader with epoch=1 and epochStartOffset=0 between 05:02:02 and 05:02:05, followed by group rebalances recorded as 'old generation 0' for groups fraud-detection and accounting at 05:02:18-05:02:20, and it continues to roll __cluster_metadata-0 segments and write KRaft snapshots every ~10-15s with metadata retention 60000 through 05:10:05.

The produce latency persists after the reconnect rather than being capped by the proxy's timeout: in the last 5 minutes the 'orders publish' histogram increase is 90.18 spans at le=+Inf, 36.64 at le=15000.0 and only 1.41 at le=10000.0, so most publishes finish above 15s.

kafka was not resource-starved while slow: its pod's memory working set is 592-622MiB against a 900Mi limit (old pod 610-628MiB), its CPU rate after startup is 0.044-0.057 cores (spike 0.459 during startup, old pod ~0.028-0.044), its CPU-throttled-period ratio in 05:10-05:15 is 0.0145, and all five nodes report MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False and Ready=True.

The errors are new in this window: the only hourly increase values the tool returned for frontend-proxy ingress error spans over the 24-hour authorized window are 2.09 (bucket ending 04:46:08) and 236.43 (bucket ending 05:16:08).

An earlier, distinct error mode existed before the alert: ingress error spans at 04:48:20 and 04:48:47 are HTTP 503 on GET requests for user_browse_product and user_view_cart with durations of only 826,374us and 425,419us, i.e. fast failures rather than the ~15s 504 checkout timeouts.

accounting shows a small concurrent latency signal consistent with Kafka: 6.23 of its spans in 05:10-05:15 exceed 5s and they are all on the 'order-consumed' Kafka consumer span (its 'orders receive' and 'otel' spans are 0), while its error-span count over the window is 0.

Application-level failure inside frontend or checkout is not what the traces show: frontend records 0 error-status spans on all its operations over the window and its POST /api/checkout span completes with http.status_code 200 (after 15.44s), and checkout's only error-status spans are on the Kafka producer span 'orders publish' (14.70). The proxy's 504s are upstream timeout symptoms, not an application error generated by frontend.

Rejected: that slow checkout dependencies other than Kafka (payment, cart, currency, email) caused the timeouts. In the same traces those spans take 13-100ms (payment charge 13,058us, cart EmptyCart 100,913us, currency Convert 14,187-17,425us, email send 2,758-3,494us) and their 10-15s span counts in 05:10-05:15 are 0.

Rejected: that CPU throttling or node pressure made frontend-proxy or checkout slow. The proxy's throttled-period ratio is 0.0389 and checkout's is 0.0 in 05:10-05:15, and no node reports MemoryPressure, DiskPressure or PIDPressure.

Primary supported cause: the kafka Deployment pod-template restart at 2026-11-15T05:00:36 (rollout restart) replaced the single broker, producing a ~2-minute broker outage (checkout connection refused / circuit breaker open) and then persistently slow produce (~15s+ per 'orders publish'), which pushed checkout PlaceOrder and frontend /api/checkout past the proxy's ~15s upstream limit and produced the 504 error spans that the alert counts. The restart is the last change before the latency onset; the exact broker-internal mechanism that keeps produce slow after 05:02:21 is not directly observed.

Remaining candidate for the persistent produce latency: the restarted broker runs with a fresh empty log directory (/tmp/kafka-logs, no PVC on the pod) and rebuilt state (KRaft election at epoch=1 with epochStartOffset=0, consumer groups rejoining from generation 0, continuous __cluster_metadata segment rolling/snapshotting with 60s retention), so produce requests may be delayed by that rebuild. Not verified: no Kafka JMX/broker-side latency metric is available in this target.

Remaining candidate: a network-path problem between checkout and the Kafka endpoint (checkout resolved kafka to 100.65.62.181 and got connection refused during the broker restart). No evidence of ongoing connection errors after 05:02:21 was found, so this is not supported as the cause of the post-reconnect slowness, but it is not fully ruled out either.

Human follow-up should confirm whether the kafka rollout restart at 05:00:36 was intentional (the restartedAt annotation is the only change in the Deployment history) and whether the ~15s+ produce latency has subsided; if it persists, investigate the broker's post-restart state and consider restarting it only under change control. No remediation was executed here.

gaps: The alerting rule itself is not visible: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data, so the exact expression and the 0.4 value's unit are inferred from matching the traces error-span rate, not read from the rule.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so it cannot be verified who or what issued the kafka pod-template restart at 2026-11-15T05:00:36Z or why.
Logs of the previous kafka pod (kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2) are gone with the deleted pod ('previous terminated container not found'), so the broker's state before the restart is unknown.

No broker-side/JMX Kafka metrics exist in this Prometheus target, and kube_pod_container_info returned no series for the kafka pod, so the internal reason produce stays above 15s after the reconnect and the image digest comparison are unverified.
The frontend pod's container logs returned 0 lines for 05:03-05:16, so frontend-side handling of the 15s checkout calls could not be inspected.
http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no series for this window, so that HTTP-level error/latency view is unknown rather than zero.

The trace evidence is a biased Jaeger sample that lags a few minutes and only holds recent traces; the 3 ingress error spans inspected all had http.status_code 504 but this sample cannot establish that all 236 error spans were 504 rather than 503.

The latency baseline comes only from the same 73-minute window (zero >10s publishes for 04:38-05:02); no earlier-day latency series was retrieved, so the pre-incident latency level beyond that is unknown.
The earlier 503 error mode seen at 04:48 (fast, on browse/cart GETs) was not traced to a cause and it is unknown whether it persisted after 04:48.
next_steps: Check the Platform/change records for an intentional 'kubectl rollout restart' of deployment/kafka in namespace otel-demo at 2026-11-15T05:00:36Z.
Re-check checkout 'orders publish' span durations and frontend-proxy ingress 504 counts after 05:16 to confirm whether the error rate is recovering now that the broker is up.

If produce latency persists, collect Kafka broker metrics (request queue, produce p99, ISR/leader state) and the current kafka pod logs beyond 05:10, which were not readable past that point in this Run.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
